glossary.definition: The request setting that decides whether the model may (auto), must (any, tool) or must not (none) call a tool.
A standard vocabulary for describing JSON data; tools use it to define their input arguments.
The id of one tool call; the result for that call must carry the same id.
A flag on a tool result saying the call failed, so the model can adjust instead of trusting the output.
The longest chain of calls that depend on each other; it sets the minimum wall-clock time.
A unique value sent with a write so the server performs it once and replays the result on retries.
Waiting longer after each failed attempt, for example 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, up to a cap.
Choosing a random wait between zero and the backoff value, so clients do not retry in step.
A lightweight remote-procedure-call format in JSON; MCP and one A2A binding use version 2.0.
MCP’s remote transport: requests are HTTP POSTs to one endpoint; replies are JSON or a request-scoped event stream.
Standard input and output; MCP’s transport for a server running as a local process.
Hints such as readOnlyHint and destructiveHint that describe a tool’s behaviour; untrusted unless the server is trusted.
A JSON document an A2A agent publishes describing its identity, skills, capabilities and how to authenticate.
An output an A2A task returns, such as a document, an estimate or a booking reference.
A tool whose definition is sent with the request but hidden from the model until a tool search finds it.
A search result that names a tool; the API expands it into the full tool definition so the model can call it.
A tool the model calls to find other tools by keyword or meaning, so large tool libraries need not be loaded in full.
Proof Key for Code Exchange: the client sends a hash of a secret verifier when it starts sign-in and the verifier itself when it redeems the code, so a stolen authorization code is useless.
An access token issued to an agent or app to act for one user, within the scopes that user consented to.
Issuing a new refresh token each time one is used and invalidating the old one, so a stolen refresh token is detected and stops working.
Encrypted storage for users’ access and refresh tokens, read by the tool layer at call time so secrets never enter the prompt.
Loading only a short description up front and the full instructions or files when they are needed.
A packaged folder of instructions, scripts and references that an agent loads when a task matches its description.

symptomRouter.symptom: The model never calls tools, or calls them with malformed arguments
symptomRouter.advice: Get the loop right: clear schemas, tool_choice auto, strict inputs, and results matched to call ids.

symptomRouter.symptom: It picks the wrong tool, fills arguments badly or drowns in output
symptomRouter.advice: Merge overlapping tools, write full descriptions, trim results and make errors actionable.

symptomRouter.symptom: Independent lookups run one after another
symptomRouter.advice: Run independent calls in one turn concurrently and return all results together.

symptomRouter.symptom: A retry could charge, refund or email twice
symptomRouter.advice: Give each action one idempotency key, reuse it on every retry, and back off with jitter.

symptomRouter.symptom: One set of tools should serve many apps and agents
symptomRouter.advice: Expose them once as an MCP server; any MCP host can discover and call them.

symptomRouter.symptom: A whole task must go to another organisation’s agent
symptomRouter.advice: Delegate it over A2A: discover the Agent Card, send a task, track its states and collect artifacts.

symptomRouter.symptom: The agent has hundreds of tools and keeps picking the wrong one
symptomRouter.advice: Keep a few common tools loaded, defer the rest behind a search tool, and write descriptions that match how people ask.

symptomRouter.symptom: The agent’s tools use one shared API key, or a token sits in the prompt
symptomRouter.advice: Give each user a delegated OAuth token with one scope per tool, keep it short-lived in a vault the model never sees, and log every call under the user.

symptomRouter.symptom: The agent needs dozens of procedures and the prompt is huge
symptomRouter.advice: Package each procedure as a skill: short description up front, instructions and scripts loaded only when needed.
